abstract:
|
  Round 5 on issue #65's citation-resolver gate: a narrow, closed-list fix cycle addressing a fresh reviewer's round-4 REJECT under the reviewer-rotation rule. The fresh reviewer confirmed the round-4 amputation had largely worked (header claims down from 5 to 1, every survivor verified, zero test-logic change confirmed mechanically) and found exactly four residual defects rather than a systemic instrument problem, so no escalation was triggered - a narrow cap instead.

  The most consequential finding (MAJOR-R4-1) was that the amputation, in cutting historical narrative, had also cut a load-bearing RULE: the historical-coordinate marker genuinely exempts a citation from both binding checks in the code, but the 32-line header no longer disclosed this, leaving an unqualified BINDING claim the code itself contradicted (the reviewer proved this live with a marked citation to a nonexistent file passing clean). This was restored precisely - not as narrative, but as the same kind of rule-only sentence the amputation intended the header to contain - and the one place in the repo that depends on this gate documenting the marker's meaning (a hook script's own comment) was checked to still resolve correctly afterward.

  The remaining three items were smaller and mechanical: a mislabeled review round in three unrelated documents (a one-word fix, repeated identically in each), a false meta-claim about where a threshold was stated (resolved by deletion rather than duplication), and one more stale calibration number in a different document, fixed by removing the number rather than replacing it with a new one that would rot the same way.

  No test logic was touched anywhere in this round, and every suite's pass/fail/skip split was confirmed identical to the pre-round-5 state: the gate itself (28/0/4/32), the full scripts/tests suite (223/0/4/227), scripts/probes (24/24), and CodeCitationPolicy.Tests.ps1 in isolation (13/13). A self-check of the diff confirmed no new digit-bearing or locative claim about the test file's own contents was introduced - the only digits added were an unchanged rule definition and the previously-mandated trigger value.
